To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) spatial econometric model specification should take into consideration the possibility of one-directional adjacency matrices and (2) spatial autocorrelation can be recognized by a spatial autoregressive (SAR) model with an adjacency matrix that is one-directional.

one-directional adjacency matrices can lead to a misinterpretation of the spatial dependence structure and that a spatial econometric model that is estimated with one-directional adjacency matrix can lead to a biased estimation of the parameters.

the one-directional adjacency matrix is a useful tool to specify the spatial structure and that spatial econometric models with one-directional adjacency matrices are more appropriate than those with reciprocal adjacency matrices in many practical cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the issue of one-directional adjacency matrices and the specification of spatial autoregressive models in spatial econometrics.
the specification of the direction of the adjacency relationship in spatial autoregressions.
the specification of spatial dependencies, and we show that the specification is important in the context of spatial autoregressive models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rook contiguity criteria are not the best choice for spatial autoregression models.
, when one-directional effects exist, the use of reciprocal adjacency matrices may lead to the wrong conclusions.
one-directional effects are not a mere theoretical curiosity, but a real and important phenomenon in the spatial context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial econometric models are not necessarily the same if the spatial dependence structure is not reciprocal.
the one-directional adjacency matrix is not necessarily a good proxy for the spatial dependence matrix in spatial autoregressions.
the spatial econometrician should consider one-directional adjacency relationships as well as reciprocal ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the specification of spatial effects should be done with caution, and that the specification should be based on the economic theory.
one-directional effects should be considered in spatial analysis.
spatial econometric models should be specified based on the nature of the data, not based on theoretical assumptions.
